the transition at zero baryon chemical potentials is a crossover, and that there is no evidence for a first order phase transition at any μB, even at the physical point, for three degenerate quarks.
the phase structure of the three flavour QCD with degenerate mass quarks at finite T and μB can be determined by a single parameter, i.e., the mass ratio mπ/mρ.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transition temperature is lowered with increasing chemical potential, and that the nature of the transition changes from a crossover to a first order transition at a finite chemical potential.
we observe a rapid crossover for a wide range of the quark mass mπ = 0.2-0.6 and the temperature T = 1.2-1.8.
the transition temperature at μB = 0 is Tc(0) = 160(2)MeV and the transition temperature increases with μB as dTc/dμB = 0.6(2) MeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase transition temperature Tc(μB) is a monotonically decreasing function of μB.
the phase structure of the three flavour QCD is very similar to the case of two flavour QCD, and the transition temperature is not very different from the case of two flavours.
the nature of transition does not depend strongly on the ratio mπ/mρ.
